correctness.rationale: The increasing prefix of v_j is emitted by the stack up to its last entry before the 1; the next larger entry (or the final flush) emits the 1 followed by that last entry. This gives v_(j−1). The translated differences have norm √(j(j+1)) and pairwise dot product zero (the j initial ones cancel the −j term against any later vector). Isotropic Gaussian scores are thus independent normals with the stated scales and with the origin also available. For k=n−j and bounded s=t_n²k/n, Mills' formula gives the tail ratio e^(−s)(1+o(1)) uniformly; the step size in s is t_n²/n. The inequality 1/a²−1≥2(k−1/2)/n follows from a=√(j(j+1))/n≤(j+1/2)/n and supplies a summable geometric majorant for the remaining layer. The total normal tail tends to e^(−x) since nφ(u)/u³ tends to e^(−x) with the stated c_n. On bounded marked rectangles the sum of rare-event probabilities converges to the product intensity; the total squared probabilities vanish since the maximal term is O(t_n²/n). The two sign bins are disjoint at one index, yielding independent Poisson limits via the same product expansion. One can truncate below a fixed low height and above a fixed large location and remove the cutoffs using the Gumbel lower tail and the geometric bound. The independent Exp(1) location marks then follow by the factorized intensities. The origin is negligible (probability 2^(−(n−1)) for each sign). Finally the chi-square radius has relative fluctuations O_P(n^(−1/2)), negligible at the t_n/√n spherical width scale, and does not change the indices.
residual_risks: Localization is on the scale n/(2 log n), not a high-probability hard bound at one multiple of that scale. Independence is only in the joint limit.
